text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- State-owned office buildings worth 10 billion dong ($900,000) or more will first have to get approval by the Prime Minister to prevent waste state funds.
-- The United Nations Development Programme will host a regional workshop in Hanoi this Friday and Saturday to examine the experiences and challenges of poverty eradication in Asia Pacific.
-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment last week licensed five projects worth $25 million, taking the total licensed so far this year to 126, valued at about $1.36 billion.
-- Vietnam will auction 70 billion dong ($5.9 million) worth of one-year Treasury notes on Wednesday.

-- The Politburo has ordered a focus on the education of the party and the people while celebrating the 80th anniversary of the Russian October Revolution and the 150th anniversary of the Communist Party manifesto.
-- Measures for 80 percent of the population to have clean water by 2000 were discussed by Vietnam and the international organisations UNFPA, UNICEF, UN, AFPPD on Monday in Hanoi.
-- There will be a ground-breaking ceremony on Tuesday for Ha Tay Brewery Plant, a $190-million joint-venture between Vietnam and Singapore to produce Tiger and Heineken beers.
-- Southern sugar refinery plants lack 30,000-40,000 tonnes of raw sugar for continuous operation and meeting demand until the sugar cane crop of 1997-1998.

-- Many joint-venture hotel projects are changing strategy, leasing apartments and business offices, because the number of foreign tourists visiting Vietnam has increased by a lower-than-expected 10 percent in the first five months of this year compared with the same period of last year.
